This page is a demonstration lab: it walks through the exercise of the course, Tasks 1 to 5, on a copy of R that runs inside the browser, but it fits no model. Every result on it was computed by the course pipeline with the code of the downloadable workspace, and the page reads it from small tables, so the page and the workspace give the same numbers. Each result sits beside the code of the workspace that produces it, shown as a block that does not run here. One part runs in full: the reproduction of Task 3, because the file that Multi100 gave the analysts may be shared publicly and the page loads it. The facilitator uses the page on the shared screen to walk through the tasks, and if your machine fails on the day you can follow the tasks here and still send your two results to the class chart. Everyone taking the course works in the downloadable workspace described on the [Setup](../../setup.qmd) page, which fits every model live; to fit a model yourself, or to try a specification or a causal graph that this page does not hold, use the workspace.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## While the R engine loads

The R engine, four packages with their dependencies (about 7.5 MB), the tables of the course and the file of the analysts (about 3 MB together) download into your browser the first time you open this page, which can take up to a minute on a slow connection. Read Task 1 while they load. You will know that the page is ready when the first code cell switches from a loading spinner to a "Run Code" button.

Keep this tab open. Your work stays in this page until you refresh it – there is nothing to install, nothing to save to disk, and no account needed.
:::

#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Lab machinery: the specification menu, its validation, and the helpers of
# Tasks 3, 4 and 5 – check_score_file(), try_spec(), my_experiments(),
# submit_exploration(), prereg(), run_spec() and report_result(). The page
# fits nothing: the result of every specification is its row of
# data/spec_curve.csv, which the course pipeline fitted with the estimator of
# the workspace (R/spec_tools.R, a copy of R/cohabitation/_tools.R), and
# data/menu_options.csv gives the reason for every option that is not on the
# curve. Both arrive with the page through its `resources:` list. The
# workspace fits the same specifications live and prints the same lines.

# ============================================================================
# CLASS CHART – the results Form, the course site and the tags
# ============================================================================
# The same block as in the helpers of the housing-audit case. The results Form
# that submit_exploration() and report_result() pre-fill: its ID and the entry
# codes of its seven fields. They belong to the Form that the cases of the
# course share, set up for the EU-frames case; a Form of its own replaces them
# here and nowhere else. The word in .case_word follows the tag in every label,
# so that the chart of this case reads only its own rows.
.form_id <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
.form_entry <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
                 t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
                 r = "entry.1660273001")
.case_word <- "cohabitation"
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/applied-replication"

# Both submissions of a participant carry one short tag inside the spec label,
# "explore: [amber-otter-42] cohabitation …", so that the participant can find
# their own marks on the class chart. The same functions sit in R/spec_tools.R
# of the workspace, which keeps the tag in a file; here it lasts for the
# browser session, and a nickname passed to either submission function sets it
# or brings it back after a reload.
.tag_words <- list(
  adj  = c("amber", "azure", "bright", "calm", "coral", "crisp", "dusky", "early",
           "fair", "gentle", "golden", "hazel", "ivory", "jade", "keen", "lively",
           "lunar", "misty", "noble", "olive", "pale", "quiet", "rapid", "rosy",
           "russet", "silver", "snowy", "solar", "sunny", "swift", "velvet", "vivid"),
  noun = c("otter", "heron", "lynx", "badger", "finch", "hare", "ibex", "kestrel",
           "lark", "marten", "newt", "owl", "puffin", "quail", "raven", "seal",
           "stoat", "tern", "vole", "wren", "bison", "crane", "dove", "egret",
           "fox", "gecko", "koala", "lemur", "moose", "panda", "robin", "swan")
)
.tag_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("tag", NULL, envir = .tag_env)

# A fresh tag, drawn without touching the random-number stream of the session.
.new_tag <- function() {
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit(if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
          else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(as.integer((as.numeric(Sys.time()) * 1000) %% 1e9) + Sys.getpid() %% 1e5)
  paste(sample(.tag_words$adj, 1), sample(.tag_words$noun, 1), sample(10:99, 1), sep = "-")
}

# A nickname reduced to lower-case ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens,
# at most 24 characters – the only form that the class chart parses.
.clean_tag <- function(x) {
  # iconv on Windows turns these into "?": the Romanian comma-below letters and the eszett
  x <- gsub("ß", "ss", chartr("ȘșȚț", "SsTt", trimws(as.character(x)[1])))
  ascii <- suppressWarnings(iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT"))
  if (!is.na(ascii)) x <- ascii
  x <- gsub("^-+|-+$", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x)))
  x <- gsub("-+$", "", substr(x, 1, 24))
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x))
    stop("A nickname needs at least one letter or digit, for example nickname = \"blue-heron\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  x
}

# The tag of this session: the nickname if one is given, otherwise the tag
# already drawn, otherwise a fresh one. Returns the tag and the one it replaced.
.class_tag <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  stored <- .tag_env$tag
  tag <- if (!is.null(nickname)) .clean_tag(nickname) else if (!is.null(stored)) stored else .new_tag()
  assign("tag", tag, envir = .tag_env)
  list(tag = tag, replaced = if (!is.null(stored) && !identical(tag, stored)) stored)
}
# ============================================================================


# ---- The menu of the curve and the label of the class chart --------------------
# As R/cohabitation/_tools.R defines them. Every combination of the options of
# SPEC_AXES is one specification of the curve (2 x 2 x 3 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 144).
SPEC_AXES <- list(
  cohorts = c("paper", "five_years"),
  horizon = c("five_years", "three_years"),
  adjust  = c("none", "age", "composition"),
  weights = c("weighted", "unweighted"),
  time    = c("linear", "yearly"),
  model   = c("mlogit", "logit", "cloglog")
)

# The free-text label that carries a specification to the class chart.
spec_line <- function(cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model) {
  sprintf("cohorts=%s horizon=%s adjust=%s weights=%s time=%s model=%s",
          cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model)
}


# ---- The menu --------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fifteen decisions in the order of the menu, each with the options that
# the curve keeps. The six decisions of SPEC_AXES keep two or more options,
# which multiply to the 144 specifications; on the other nine the curve keeps
# one. Every other option is a row of data/menu_options.csv, whose reason the
# helpers print when it is asked for.
.menu <- list(
  # Level 1 – Estimands
  comparison = "1995_2006",
  cohorts    = SPEC_AXES$cohorts,
  horizon    = SPEC_AXES$horizon,
  outcome    = "marriage",
  adjust     = SPEC_AXES$adjust,
  weights    = SPEC_AXES$weights,
  sample     = "paper",
  # Level 2 – Measurement
  histories  = "rebuilt",
  education  = "paper",
  short      = "drop",
  # Level 3 – Estimation
  unit       = "person_months",
  time       = SPEC_AXES$time,
  model      = SPEC_AXES$model,
  errors     = "design",
  scale      = "log_ratio"
)
.level_titles <- c(estimand    = "Level 1 – Estimands",
                   measurement = "Level 2 – Measurement",
                   estimation  = "Level 3 – Estimation")


# ---- The shipped files -----------------------------------------------------------
# Each file is read once and cached. The base reader adds nothing to the
# download of the page, and reads empty cells as NA, as readr does.
.cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.read_once <- function(name, path, ...) {
  if (is.null(.cache[[name]])) {
    if (!file.exists(path))
      stop(sprintf("%s is missing – the page loads it through its resources list. Reload the page.",
                   path), call. = FALSE)
    assign(name, utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8", # r-style: keep – the base reader adds nothing to the download
                                 na.strings = c("", "NA"), ...),
           envir = .cache)
  }
  .cache[[name]]
}
.curve   <- function() .read_once("curve", "data/spec_curve.csv")
.options <- function() .read_once("options", "data/menu_options.csv")


# ---- Pages of the course site ----------------------------------------------------
.pages <- c(
  "cases/cohabitation/index.qmd"      = "Case study",
  "cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd"       = "Specification menu",
  "cases/cohabitation/map.qmd"        = "Decision map",
  "cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd" = "Multiverse",
  "companion/event-history.qmd"       = "Event-history analysis",
  "companion/binary-outcomes.qmd"     = "Binary outcomes",
  "companion/dags.qmd"                = "Causal graphs and adjustment sets",
  "companion/weighting.qmd"           = "Weights",
  "companion/multiverse.qmd"          = "The multiverse and its critics")
.page_ref <- function(path) {
  title <- if (path %in% names(.pages)) .pages[[path]] else path
  sprintf("%s, %s/%s", title, .course_url, sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", path))
}
.or_list <- function(x) {
  q <- paste0("\"", x, "\"")
  if (length(q) == 1) q else paste(paste(q[-length(q)], collapse = ", "), "or", q[length(q)])
}


# ---- Validation ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices() reads the fifteen
# my_* choices of the preregistration cell. An option that is not on the
# curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the page of the course
# site that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve. The rows are
# found with datawizard::data_match(), which takes the values to match as a
# list and so works inside a function; remove_na = FALSE, because with its
# default it drops incomplete rows before matching and can return the wrong
# rows.
.on_menu <- function(axis, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[axis]]

.refuse <- function(axis, v, as_args) {
  shown <- if (as_args) axis else paste0("my_", axis)
  keep  <- .menu[[axis]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("cases/cohabitation/map.qmd"))
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".", shown, shown, keep[1]),
         call. = FALSE)
  opts <- .options()
  row  <- datawizard::data_match(opts, list(axis = axis, option = v), remove_na = FALSE)
  off  <- datawizard::data_match(opts, list(axis = axis, on_curve = FALSE), remove_na = FALSE)$option
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of %d specifications, so it has no result here.",
            shown, v, row$label, nrow(.curve())),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown, .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown, v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(keep, collapse = " | ")),
    if (length(off) > 0)
      sprintf("  Off the curve, refused with the reason why: %s.", paste(off, collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  bad <- purrr::discard(names(.menu), \(a) .on_menu(a, ch[[a]]))
  if (length(bad) > 0) .refuse(bad[1], ch[[bad[1]]], as_args)
  ch[names(.menu)]
}

# The choices are looked up from the frame of this function outwards, which
# reaches the session in which the preregistration cell was run.
.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- paste0("my_", names(.menu))
  ch <- mget(need, envir = environment(), inherits = TRUE, ifnotfound = list(NULL))
  missing <- need[purrr::map_lgl(ch, is.null)]
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration cell and run it first.", call. = FALSE)
  .validate(stats::setNames(ch, names(.menu)))
}


# ---- The result of a specification ------------------------------------------------
# The row of data/spec_curve.csv for the six decisions that vary on the curve:
# the estimate with its design-based test, the conventional test, the counts
# and the partial r, as the estimator of the workspace computes them; the 95%
# interval of the estimate (t on the design-based df), computed here as the
# workspace computes it; and its place among the 144.
.result <- function(ch) {
  curve <- .curve()
  stored <- datawizard::data_match(curve, ch[c("cohorts", "horizon", "adjust", "weights", "time", "model")],
                                   remove_na = FALSE)
  if (nrow(stored) != 1)
    stop("This specification has no row in data/spec_curve.csv; reload the page.", call. = FALSE)
  crit <- stats::qt(0.975, stored$df)
  c(as.list(stored), list(ci_low = stored$b - crit * stored$se, ci_high = stored$b + crit * stored$se,
                          further = sum(curve$b < stored$b - 1e-9), n_curve = nrow(curve)))
}


# ---- The printout ----------------------------------------------------------------
.fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 1e-4) "< 0.0001" else sprintf("= %s", format(signif(p, 2), scientific = FALSE))
.fmt_n <- function(n) format(round(n), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

.class_line <- function(res) {
  below <- res$b < 0
  sig   <- res$p < 0.05
  if (below && sig) "below zero and significant at 5%, in the direction of the claim"
  else if (below) "below zero, but not significant at 5%"
  else if (sig) "above zero and significant at 5%, against the direction of the claim"
  else "above zero and not significant at 5%"
}

.print_result <- function(ch, res, lead = NULL) {
  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    paste0("  ", spec_line(ch$cohorts, ch$horizon, ch$adjust, ch$weights, ch$time, ch$model)),
    sprintf("  Estimate: %.3f on the log scale, 95%% interval %.3f to %.3f",
            res$b, res$ci_low, res$ci_high),
    sprintf("            the later cohort married at %.2f times the monthly chance of the earlier one",
            res$ratio),
    sprintf("  Test: t = %.2f on %d df, p %s (design-based errors, from the strata and clusters of both surveys)",
            res$stat, round(res$df), .fmt_p(res$p)),
    sprintf("        conventional errors, which treat every person-month as independent: z = %.2f",
            res$z_model),
    sprintf("  n = %s person-months of %s unions, %s marriages; partial r = %.3f (the conversion rule of Multi100)",
            .fmt_n(res$n), .fmt_n(res$n_unions), .fmt_n(res$n_marriages), res$r),
    paste0("  Verdict: ", .class_line(res)),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %d of the %d specifications have an estimate further below zero",
            res$further, res$n_curve)))
  invisible(res)
}


# ---- Task 3: the file that Multi100 gave the analysts ---------------------------
# The person-month file that SCORE built for its replication of the paper and
# that Multi100 gave each of the five analysts: 70,188 rows of 3,963 women from
# five surveys, osf.io/b6p3j, there named "Estimation Data - Kuo (JWzJ).csv".
# The page loads it unchanged, under a course name. check_score_file()
# compares its MD5 sum, a short code computed from the contents of a file that
# changes if a single byte of it changes, with that of the copy on the OSF.
.score <- list(path = "data/score_person_months.csv",
               md5  = "2b656d3814d273f4a93e29bc4f0139ef",
               url  = "https://osf.io/b6p3j/")

check_score_file <- function() {
  f <- .score
  ok <- file.exists(f$path) && unname(tools::md5sum(f$path)) == f$md5
  writeLines(if (ok) {
    sprintf("%s is the file that Multi100 gave the analysts: its MD5 sum matches the copy on the OSF.",
            f$path)
  } else {
    c(sprintf("%s is missing, or it is not the file that Multi100 gave the analysts.", f$path),
      "  Reload the page, which loads the file again through its resources list.")
  })
  invisible(ok)
}


# ---- Task 4: the exploratory helpers -----------------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("log", NULL, envir = .tried)
assign("last", NULL, envir = .tried)

# The first six arguments are the decisions on which the curve keeps more
# than one option, in the order of the menu; the other nine are fixed on the
# curve, and asking for any other option of theirs prints the reason why it is
# not on the curve.
try_spec <- function(cohorts = "paper", horizon = "five_years", adjust = "composition",
                     weights = "weighted", time = "linear", model = "mlogit",
                     comparison = "1995_2006", outcome = "marriage", sample = "paper",
                     histories = "rebuilt", education = "paper", short = "drop",
                     unit = "person_months", errors = "design", scale = "log_ratio") {
  ch <- .validate(list(comparison = comparison, cohorts = cohorts, horizon = horizon,
                       outcome = outcome, adjust = adjust, weights = weights, sample = sample,
                       histories = histories, education = education, short = short,
                       unit = unit, time = time, model = model, errors = errors, scale = scale),
                  as_args = TRUE)
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, lead = "")
  row <- data.frame(ch, b = res$b, ratio = res$ratio, ci_low = res$ci_low, ci_high = res$ci_high,  # r-style: keep – data.frame() spreads the list of choices into columns
                    t = res$stat, p = res$p, n = res$n, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  assign("log", if (is.null(.tried$log)) row else datawizard::data_merge(.tried$log, row, join = "bind"),
         envir = .tried)
  assign("last", list(ch = ch, res = res), envir = .tried)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything that try_spec() has looked up. Only the
# decisions that varied are shown; the others are those of the reference
# specification. The datawizard verbs here name only columns of the log, which
# they can see from inside a function.
my_experiments <- function() {
  d <- .tried$log
  if (is.null(d)) {
    writeLines("Nothing tried yet – call try_spec() at least once.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  varied <- purrr::keep(names(.menu), \(a) length(unique(d[[a]])) > 1)
  show <- d |>
    datawizard::data_modify(estimate = round(b, 3),
                            ratio = round(ratio, 2),
                            interval = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", ci_low, ci_high),
                            t = round(t, 2)) |>
    datawizard::data_select(c(varied, "estimate", "ratio", "interval", "t", "n"))
  writeLines(sprintf("Specifications you have tried (%d), estimates on the log scale:\n", nrow(d)))
  # wide enough for all six varied decisions on one line
  old_width <- options(width = max(getOption("width"), 130))
  on.exit(options(old_width))
  print(show, row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(sprintf("\nEstimates from %.3f to %.3f  |  below zero and significant at 5%%: %d of %d",
                     min(d$b), max(d$b), sum(d$b < 0 & d$p < 0.05), nrow(d)))
  invisible(show)
}

submit_exploration <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(.tried$last))
    stop("Nothing to submit – call try_spec() first, ending with the specification you want on the chart.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .submit(.tried$last$ch, .tried$last$res, "explore",
          "Your exploratory submission (the last specification you tried):", nickname)
}


# ---- Task 5: the declared helpers --------------------------------------------------
# prereg() prints the cell and returns it, so that run_spec() can check that
# the cell has not changed since. The estimand statement is assembled from
# the phrase column of menu_options.csv, in the order that its codebook sets;
# the row of each choice is found in the order of the menu.
prereg <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  rows <- purrr::imap(ch, \(option, axis) datawizard::data_match(.options(), list(axis = axis, option = option),
                                                                 remove_na = FALSE)) |>
    purrr::list_rbind() |>
    datawizard::data_modify(line = sprintf("    %-20s : %-13s (%s)", decision, option, label))
  block <- purrr::imap(.level_titles, \(title, lv) c(paste0("  ", title), rows$line[rows$level == lv])) |>
    unlist(use.names = FALSE)
  ph <- stats::setNames(rows$phrase, rows$axis)
  statement <- c(
    sprintf("%s%s, %s %s, the change in %s %s, %s, %s (%s, %s, %s).",
            toupper(substr(ph[["sample"]], 1, 1)), substring(ph[["sample"]], 2), ph[["cohorts"]],
            ph[["comparison"]], ph[["outcome"]], ph[["horizon"]], ph[["weights"]], ph[["adjust"]],
            ph[["histories"]], ph[["education"]], ph[["short"]]),
    sprintf("%s %s, %s, %s %s.", ph[["model"]], ph[["unit"]], ph[["time"]], ph[["errors"]],
            ph[["scale"]]))
  writeLines(c(
    "DECLARED – your preregistered specification, fixed before it is fitted:",
    "",
    block,
    "",
    "  The estimand statement",
    strwrap(statement, width = 78, indent = 4, exdent = 4),
    "",
    "run_spec() and report_result() read these choices from here. Copied into",
    "your notes, this cell is your preregistration."))
  invisible(structure(list(choices = ch), class = "cohabitation_prereg"))
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "cohabitation_prereg"))
    stop("Pass the object that prereg() returned: my_spec <- prereg(), then run_spec(my_spec).",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!identical(spec$choices, .check_choices()))
    stop("The preregistration cell has changed since prereg() returned this object. Run the whole cell again, then run_spec(my_spec).",
         call. = FALSE)
  .print_result(spec$choices, .result(spec$choices),
                "Your preregistered specification, as the course pipeline fitted it:")
}

report_result <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  .submit(ch, .result(ch), "declared",
          "Your declared submission (straight from your preregistration):", nickname)
}


# ---- Submission ------------------------------------------------------------------
# One submission, used by both phases. The phase, the tag and the word of the
# case are prefixed to the free-text spec label, which carries the six
# decisions that vary on the curve. The estimate and its standard error are
# sent on the log scale, the t of the design-based errors with its df, the
# person-months as n, and r by the rule of Multi100 from the conventional z,
# as the r column of spec_curve.csv holds it.
.submit <- function(ch, res, phase, lead, nickname = NULL) {
  tg <- .class_tag(nickname)
  spec_label <- paste0(phase, ": [", tg$tag, "] ", .case_word, " ",
                       spec_line(ch$cohorts, ch$horizon, ch$adjust, ch$weights, ch$time, ch$model))
  value <- c(spec = spec_label, b = sprintf("%.5f", res$b), se = sprintf("%.5f", res$se),
             t = sprintf("%.3f", res$stat), df = as.character(round(res$df)),
             n = as.character(res$n), r = sprintf("%.3f", res$r))
  query <- purrr::imap_chr(.form_entry, \(entry, k)
    paste0(entry, "=", utils::URLencode(value[[k]], reserved = TRUE))) |>
    paste(collapse = "&")
  url <- sprintf("https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/%s/viewform?usp=pp_url&%s", .form_id, query)

  writeLines(c(
    lead,

## Task 2, continued – The estimand and the graph {#task-2-estimand-and-graph}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template that you can adapt [@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand]:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is, for each cohabiting union, in each month in which it is still intact, whether the couple marries in that month. The **target population** is the first cohabitations that came before any marriage, of women aged 15–44 in the United States. The estimand compares the average of that quantity in unions begun in 2005–2010 with unions begun in 1990–1995, either as the two cohorts were or for women of the same age at the start, race-ethnicity and education.

Nobody can assign the period in which a union begins, so the estimand is a comparison of two populations of unions rather than of one union under two conditions, and whether the change in who cohabits belongs to the answer is the decision that the last clause of the template leaves open. A causal graph sets this out. A graph of this kind is a diagram of what causes what: variables are nodes, arrows run from cause to effect, and the rules for reading the graph say which paths between the period and marriage are open, given what the comparison holds constant. The graph below is written in ordinary R, one arrow per string, each written the way it is drawn, so that `"education -> marriage"` is the arrow from education to the chance that a cohabiting couple marries. Education and race-ethnicity shape both whether a woman cohabits at all (`cohabits`) and whether a cohabiting couple marries; the age at which the couple moved in (`age_start`) shapes marriage too; and the period shapes who cohabits, because cohabitation spread. One arrow is switched off with a `#`, the arrow from the period to marriage, which is the change that the claim is about.


::: {.cell autorun='true'}
```{webr}

# line between them and the selection into cohabitation below it. A node
# without a position here is drawn on a row below the graph.
.dag_xy <- list(period = c(0, 0), marriage = c(4, 0), race = c(1.2, 1.6),
                education = c(2.6, 1.8), age_start = c(3.6, 1.1), cohabits = c(2, -1.4))

# A graph from arrows written "cause -> effect", one per string. The named
# arguments come last, so that switching off the last arrow with a # never
# leaves a comma dangling. The arrows, sorted, are the key under which
# data/dag_answers.csv holds the answers for the graph.
make_dag <- function(..., exposure = "period", outcome = "marriage", latent = character(0)) {
  arrows <- c(...)
  ends <- purrr::map(arrows, \(a) {
    e <- trimws(strsplit(a, "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
    if (length(e) < 2 || !all(nzchar(e)) || grepl("<-", a, fixed = TRUE))
      stop(sprintf("Write each arrow as \"cause -> effect\", for example \"education -> marriage\"; \"%s\" is not one.",
                   a), call. = FALSE)
    e
  })
  from <- unlist(purrr::map(ends, \(e) e[-length(e)]))
  to <- unlist(purrr::map(ends, \(e) e[-1]))
  drawn <- paste(from, to, sep = " -> ")
  structure(list(edges = list(from = from[!duplicated(drawn)], to = to[!duplicated(drawn)]),
                 nodes = unique(c(exposure, outcome, from, to)),
                 exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome, latent = latent,
                 key = paste(sort(unique(drawn), method = "radix"), collapse = "; ")),
            class = "simple_dag")
}

# The figure. Colour marks the exposure and the outcome. Each arrow stops at
# the edge of the box of its target, which is sized from the length of the name.
plot_dag <- function(d) {
  x <- purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) if (v %in% names(.dag_xy)) .dag_xy[[v]][1] else NA_real_)
  y <- purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) if (v %in% names(.dag_xy)) .dag_xy[[v]][2] else NA_real_)
  unplaced <- is.na(x)
  x <- replace(x, unplaced, 1.2 * (cumsum(unplaced)[unplaced] - 1))
  y <- replace(y, unplaced, -3)
  half_w <- 0.06 + 0.032 * nchar(d$nodes)
  role <- factor(datawizard::recode_into(d$nodes %in% d$exposure ~ "exposure",
                                         d$nodes %in% d$outcome ~ "outcome",
                                         d$nodes %in% d$latent ~ "unobserved",
                                         default = "observed"),
                 levels = c("exposure", "outcome", "observed", "unobserved"))
  # how far along a unit vector (ux, uy) the edge of a box of half-width w lies
  to_edge <- \(ux, uy, w) pmin(w / pmax(abs(ux), 1e-9), 0.15 / pmax(abs(uy), 1e-9))
  tail <- match(d$edges$from, d$nodes)
  head <- match(d$edges$to, d$nodes)
  len <- sqrt((x[head] - x[tail])^2 + (y[head] - y[tail])^2)
  ux <- (x[head] - x[tail]) / len
  uy <- (y[head] - y[tail]) / len
  s0 <- to_edge(ux, uy, half_w[tail])
  s1 <- to_edge(ux, uy, half_w[head]) + 0.04

  # the boxes, coloured by role; tinyplot has no type for arrows, so they go
  # on the same canvas through graphics::arrows(); then the names, white on
  # the coloured boxes and dark on the pale one
  tinyplot::tinyplot(xmin = x - half_w, xmax = x + half_w, ymin = y - 0.13, ymax = y + 0.13,
                     by = role, type = "rect",
                     palette = c("#1b6ca8", "#d1495b", "grey45", "grey88"), fill = "by",
                     legend = list("bottom!", title = NULL), axes = FALSE, frame.plot = FALSE,
                     xlab = NA, ylab = NA,
                     xlim = range(x) + c(-0.45, 0.45), ylim = range(y) + c(-0.3, 0.3),
                     grid = FALSE, theme = "minimal")
  graphics::arrows(x[tail] + s0 * ux, y[tail] + s0 * uy, x[head] - s1 * ux, y[head] - s1 * uy,
                   length = 0.1, angle = 20, col = "grey40", lwd = 1.5)
  tinyplot::tinyplot(x = x, y = y, by = role,
                     type = tinyplot::type_text(labels = d$nodes, font = 2),
                     palette = c("white", "white", "white", "grey25"), cex = 0.8, add = TRUE)
}

  "education -> cohabits",
  "race -> cohabits",
  # Education and race-ethnicity shape whether a cohabiting couple marries.
  "education -> marriage",
  "race -> marriage",
  # The age at which the couple moved in; if you think that the later cohort
  # moved in at a different age, take the # off the third line.
  "education -> age_start",
  "age_start -> marriage",
  # "period -> age_start",

  # The change that the claim is about: take the # off if you believe it.
  # "period -> marriage",

  exposure = "period", outcome = "marriage"

adjustmentSets(my_dag)                                 # r-style: keep – the function of this page, which prints the answer of dagitty
paths(my_dag, Z = "cohabits")                          # r-style: keep – as above

```
:::


`adjustmentSets()` returns the empty set, which dagitty prints as `{}`: nothing in the graph causes the period in which a union began, so among all women the comparison of periods needs nothing held constant. The three paths between the period and marriage all run through `cohabits`, a common effect of the period, of education and of race-ethnicity (a collider), and without any conditioning they are closed. Keeping only cohabitors conditions on that collider and opens all three: among cohabitors, the period goes with education and race-ethnicity, because the mix of women who cohabit changed, as the shares above showed. Holding education and race-ethnicity constant as well closes the three paths again.

Now take the `#` off the arrow `"period -> marriage"` and run the cell again. Then take the `#` off `"period -> age_start"` as well. Answer three questions for your own notes: which paths are open under the selection alone and which once education and race-ethnicity are held constant; what the age at the start becomes once the period shapes it, and what holding it constant then estimates; and which of the adjustment sets of the menu answers which question.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answers

1.  Under the selection alone, the arrow of the claim and the three paths through education and race-ethnicity are open; with education and race-ethnicity held constant, the arrow of the claim alone. The difference between the two comparisons is the change in who cohabits.
2.  A mediator: part of the change would run through a change in the age at which couples moved in, and holding it constant removes that part. In these data the mean age at the start was 22.0 in both cohorts, so the path carries little.
3.  No adjustment answers the claim about cohabitors as they were, the change in who cohabits included. Age, race-ethnicity and education answer it for cohabitors of the same characteristics, the change in behaviour within groups. Both are readings of "cohabitors" that a careful analyst could hold.

The three adjustment sets of the menu follow the graph: nothing besides the time since the start of the union (`"none"`), the age at the start and its square (`"age"`), and those with race-ethnicity and education, the controls of the paper without its interactions (`"composition"`). The adjustment set is the third argument of `try_spec()` in Task 4, and whatever you conclude here belongs in field 4 of your preregistration in Task 5.
